open_points.subject: A19-1
open_points.text: render(v) = escape(v) for every stored value v   -- A19-1
open_points.question: Does A19-1 quantify over every value Registry stores, including non-text runtime values such as the uploaded file, or only over stored text when it is rendered into an owner page?
options: Every stored value must have a text rendering covered by the invariant.
The invariant applies only when a stored value is displayed.
The invariant applies only to stored values whose model type is text.
open_points.default_guess: Apply it to every stored value that the owner interface displays, and restate the invariant conditionally.

witness.initial: An owner session holds an uploaded export containing arbitrary bytes, while its page shows only a digest and parsed mapping fields.
events: The owner uploads a file containing bytes that are not valid text.
outcomes: A19-1 requires a defined escaped rendering of the raw uploaded value.
A19-1 applies only to the digest and parsed text actually displayed; the raw file needs no rendering.
witness.observer: The test author deciding which values the A19-1 witness must exercise.

open_points.subject: A19 Required test 5
open_points.question: Does this mean the raw uploaded file is included, every stored text value parsed from the file is included, or only file-derived values that a page happens to display?
options: Exercise the raw file as a rendered value.
Exercise every imported text field after parsing and storage.
Exercise only imported fields displayed by the selected pages.
open_points.default_guess: It means every imported text field that can be displayed, not the raw upload bytes.

witness.initial: The import file contains a display name with the five named characters and also contains opaque non-text bytes permitted by its eventual format.
events: Registry renders the mapping and, after acceptance, the imported project's page.
outcomes: The required test must render or otherwise account for the raw file itself.
The required test need only check the parsed display name in each applicable output context.
witness.observer: The factory check and later page-test generator.

open_points.subject: A19-2 Required tests 5 and 6
open_points.text: so this shows it for every value given or imported.
open_points.question: What must the Required tests show to establish A19-2 for all evaluation and execution paths, rather than only browser rendering and one store-query example?
options: Show that every caller-supplied and imported value reaches no query, command, template, evaluator or executable sink as structure, including selectors checked against closed lists.
Limit A19-2 to browser and store-query interpretation and narrow the invariant accordingly.
Add separate required evidence for import parsing, command-like sinks, template construction and closed-alternative selectors.
open_points.default_guess: Keep the universal invariant and require evidence covering every interpreted sink plus closed-list selectors.

witness.initial: An implementation parameterizes store writes and safely escapes HTML, but a later operation interpolates an imported value into a command or template.
events: The operation containing the other interpreted sink is generated.
outcomes: The stated witnesses are treated as sufficient and the build passes.
A19-2 requires that additional sink to be checked, and the build is refused.
witness.observer: The factory gate deciding whether A19-2 has been demonstrated.

open_points.subject: A19 Required test 5
open_points.text: Every page is made by one renderer, so this shows it for every stored value, whoever wrote it and whichever way it came in, the import file's included.
open_points.question: What later check establishes that every owner page and every output context actually passes through the common renderer, including pages added after this test is written?
options: A factory check enumerates all owner routes and verifies that each delegates to the renderer.
Generation makes owner pages constructible only through the renderer, and a structural check enforces that boundary.
Tests render an explicit page census that must be updated whenever routes change.
open_points.default_guess: Enforce renderer-only page construction structurally and have a factory check enumerate all owner routes.
consequences: Route enumeration detects a bypass directly but must remain synchronized with routing.
Construction-by-type prevents ordinary bypasses but requires the generator to impose a renderer boundary.
A page census is simple but can silently omit a newly added route unless completeness is checked separately.
open_points.requirement:
The owner interface renders every stored value as text: escaped for the
   place it appears in, never as markup or script, whoever wrote it.

open_points.subject: A19 Required test 5
open_points.text: shown as that text when the value holds `<`, `>`, `&`, `"` and `'`
open_points.question: For an attribute value or link query, does “shown as that text” mean equality after HTML and URL decoding, equality of the browser-visible value, or an exact serialized byte representation?
options: Compare the parsed DOM value and decoded query value with the original text.
Compare only what a browser visibly presents to the owner.
Require a particular HTML-entity and percent-encoding serialization.
open_points.default_guess: Compare semantic values after standards-compliant parsing and decoding while separately asserting that no element or attribute was created from the value.
consequences: Semantic comparison permits equivalent safe encodings and tests the boundary guarantee.
Visible-text comparison may miss differences in hidden fields and query values.
Exact serialization makes one encoder's spelling contractual even though several encodings are equally safe.
open_points.requirement:
The owner interface renders every stored value as text: escaped for the
   place it appears in, never as markup or script, whoever wrote it.

open_points.subject: A19 Required test 6
open_points.text: Every value reaches the store through the one statement backend the specification fixes, which fills value places only (rule 3), so this shows it for every value given or imported.
open_points.question: Which generated backend is “the one statement backend,” and must generation provide one shared write path literally, or may it generate several backends if every one preserves the value-place guarantee?
options: Generate one shared statement backend used by every store write.
Generate several operation-specific statement backends and verify each one.
Generate one facade over several internal backends and treat the facade as the single specified boundary.
open_points.default_guess: Generate one specified persistence facade and allow hidden internal backends only when a factory check proves that all writes pass through the facade as value parameters.
consequences: One shared backend makes the universal argument direct but couples all persistence operations.
Several backends preserve modularity but require complete per-backend coverage.
A facade preserves a single auditable boundary while leaving internal lowering flexible.
open_points.requirement:
A value a caller gives only ever fills a value place of a query or command
   whose structure the release fixes; it never becomes an identifier, an
   operator or syntax. A value that selects among fixed alternatives — a list
   order, a type — is checked against its closed list first. How the store's
   backend lowers this is the backend's.
